intent: Execute another two candidate-specific DEVELOPMENT readiness checks *inside the same real GitHub-run* using the outcomes of F118's first two actions; carry all four action outcomes to subsequent genuine scheduled run under existing F118 source-bound state protocol.

frozen_algorithm.first_round_source: same-run F118 state.json from current GitHub SHA, event, and run ID, matching current advisory IDs and complete per-lane history; do not accept external JSON as previous result
frozen_algorithm.second_round: one additional action per Wingless/Yggdrasil, ordered Wingless then Yggdrasil; fail retry once if previous action FAIL/TIMEOUT with consecutive_failures=1; otherwise pick least-tried DIFFERENT candidate
frozen_algorithm.approved_execution: re-use F118 allowlisted native Go package tests; 90-second timeout each, record PASS/FAIL/TIMEOUT stdout_sha256 and exit_code
frozen_algorithm.retained_f118_report: keep untouched first-round state with SHA256 in separate first-round artifact
frozen_algorithm.carry_to_next_scheduled_main: replace F118 state.json with same-schema source/run/event-bound second-round state having history updated with all four executions, generation incremented by 2, two second-round evaluations, no extra authority
frozen_algorithm.within_run_report: F119 source-bound report proving both rounds four actions, transitions and next-run feedback

performance_evidence: Go package tests are real development readiness tests; fixed model-free proposal identities are UNTESTED mechanisms. A passing development check cannot become scientific candidate validation.
negative_handling: any failure and timeout preserved in BOTH rounds; even a failed check can be an operationally qualified feedback outcome, not scientific acceptance
